title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams

title: The Last Wish
author: Andrzej Sapkowski
summary: Short stories that introduce Geralt of Rivia, a witcher who hunts monsters for money and keeps finding that the people who hire him are the real danger.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling

title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
author: Scott Lynch
summary: In the canal city of Camorr, the orphan thief Locke Lamora and his gang con the nobility, until a mysterious rival starts killing the city's crime bosses.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
summary: A disgraced journalist and a brilliant, guarded hacker investigate the decades-old disappearance of a girl from one of Sweden's richest families.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: A poor former student in St Petersburg murders a pawnbroker to prove he stands above morality, and is slowly undone by guilt and a patient investigator.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: Three brothers and their dissolute father in a provincial Russian town: a murder, a trial and Dostoevsky's deepest questions about faith, doubt and free will.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
summary: An ageing Spanish gentleman reads so many tales of chivalry that he sets out as a knight-errant with his squire Sancho Panza, tilting at windmills.

title: The Doll
author: Bolesław Prus
summary: In 1870s Warsaw the self-made merchant Stanisław Wokulski ruins himself for the love of an aristocrat, in a panorama of a society torn between old and new.

title: Rosemary's Baby
author: Ira Levin
summary: A young wife in a Manhattan apartment building begins to suspect that her charming elderly neighbours and her ambitious husband have plans for her unborn child.

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
summary: A London lawyer investigates the link between his respected friend Dr Jekyll and the brutal Edward Hyde, in the classic tale of a divided self.

title: Doctor Zhivago
author: Boris Pasternak
summary: A physician and poet lives through the Russian Revolution and civil war, torn between his wife and his love for Lara.

title: North and South
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
summary: Margaret Hale moves from the rural south of England to an industrial northern town and clashes with the mill owner John Thornton over workers' rights, and over love.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
summary: A pilot stranded in the Sahara meets a little prince from a tiny asteroid, whose travels among strange grown-ups show that what matters most is invisible to the eye.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
author: C. S. Lewis

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
summary: Mole, Rat, Badger and the reckless, motor-car-mad Toad share friendship and adventures along an English river.

title: Pippi Longstocking
author: Astrid Lindgren
summary: The strongest girl in the world lives alone with a horse and a monkey, without any rules, and turns her small Swedish town upside down.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank

title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich
author: William L. Shirer

title: A People's History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn

title: God's Playground
author: Norman Davies
summary: A history of Poland from its origins to the present: the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, the partitions, the world wars and communism.

title: The Gulag Archipelago
author: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
summary: A history of the Soviet forced-labour camps, built from Solzhenitsyn's own imprisonment and the testimony of hundreds of former prisoners.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot

title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson

title: Silent Spring
author: Rachel Carson
summary: An investigation of how synthetic pesticides such as DDT poison wildlife and people, which launched the modern environmental movement.

title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson

title: Beyond Good and Evil
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
summary: Nietzsche attacks the dogmatism of earlier philosophers and of conventional morality, and sketches the free spirits of a philosophy of the future.

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
summary: The prophet Zarathustra comes down from the mountains to preach the death of God, the overman and the eternal recurrence, in poetic, biblical prose.

title: Critique of Pure Reason
author: Immanuel Kant
summary: Kant examines what reason can know independently of experience, arguing that space, time and causality are forms the mind imposes on the world.

title: The Social Contract
author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
summary: Rousseau argues that legitimate political authority can only come from an agreement among free citizens, expressed through the general will.

title: Sophie's World
author: Jostein Gaarder
summary: A Norwegian schoolgirl receives mysterious letters that lead her through the history of Western philosophy, from Socrates to Sartre, inside a puzzling novel.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
summary: A psychiatrist's account of surviving the Nazi concentration camps, and the therapy he built on it: the human drive to find meaning even in suffering.

title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
author: Robert M. Pirsig

title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
author: Maya Angelou

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty
summary: Using two centuries of tax and income data, Piketty shows that the return on capital tends to exceed economic growth, so wealth concentrates unless policy intervenes.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt, Stephen J. Dubner

title: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money
author: John Maynard Keynes
summary: Keynes argues that economies can stay stuck with high unemployment because demand is too low, and that governments should act to raise it.

title: Capital
author: Karl Marx
summary: Marx analyses capitalism as a system built on extracting surplus value from labour, and traces its tendencies toward crisis and concentration.

title: Nudge
author: Richard H. Thaler, Cass R. Sunstein

title: The C Programming Language
author: Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis M. Ritchie

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
author: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman

title: Working Effectively with Legacy Code
author: Michael C. Feathers
summary: Techniques for safely changing large codebases that have no tests: finding seams, breaking dependencies and getting code under test before refactoring it.

title: Domain-Driven Design
author: Eric Evans
summary: How to tackle complex software by modelling the business domain together with experts: ubiquitous language, entities, aggregates and bounded contexts.

title: Head First Design Patterns
author: Eric Freeman, Elisabeth Robson
summary: A visual, conversational introduction to object-oriented design patterns such as Strategy, Observer, Decorator and Factory, with Java examples.

title: Effective Java
author: Joshua Bloch
summary: Best-practice advice for the Java language and libraries: object creation, generics, enums, lambdas and streams, concurrency and API design.

title: JavaScript: The Good Parts
author: Douglas Crockford
summary: Crockford separates the elegant core of JavaScript, its functions, objects and closures, from the parts of the language that are better avoided.

title: Python Crash Course
author: Eric Matthes
summary: A hands-on introduction to programming in Python, from the basics to three projects: a game, data visualisations and a web application.

title: Fluent Python
author: Luciano Ramalho
summary: A deep tour of idiomatic Python: the data model, sequences, functions as objects, iterators and generators, concurrency and metaprogramming.

title: Clean Architecture
author: Robert C. Martin
summary: Principles for structuring software so that business rules stay independent of frameworks, databases and user interfaces.

title: The Art of Computer Programming
author: Donald E. Knuth
summary: Knuth's multi-volume treatise on algorithms and their mathematical analysis: fundamental algorithms, seminumerical algorithms, sorting and searching.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Stuart Russell, Peter Norvig
summary: The standard textbook on artificial intelligence: intelligent agents, search, logic, planning, probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, language and robotics.

title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
author: Christopher M. Bishop
summary: A machine learning textbook written from a Bayesian perspective: probability distributions, linear models, kernel methods, graphical models and approximate inference.

title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
author: Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman

title: Machine Learning
author: Tom M. Mitchell
summary: An introductory textbook covering concept learning, decision trees, neural networks, Bayesian learning, instance-based learning and reinforcement learning.
